observations: The adopted row carries the guard this tester asked for and it earned its place on the first run: without it, a green row would also be what a window that never opened looks like, and my own 900-paragraph version passed against defective code for exactly that reason. In the red run the guard reported 65 part-built samples and 122 frame-text samples; a future node fast enough to paint 4,000 paragraphs in two batches will now fail the row by name instead of passing quietly.

The write row's move into heavy-document-writes.e2e.ts with a block-index drain explains noise I measured in round 5: the 8,000-item body is 8,001 blocks and its half 4,001, both past the 2,000-block deferral, so a reconciliation tick was landing on a later timed write. My round-5 pairs drained the settlement but not the index.

Timing discipline on this pod still decides this row: the implementer saw 1,039 ms once in five quiet Chromium runs and 1,621 and 3,897 ms on a pod running other work. Every number above was taken with nothing else of mine or theirs running.
